lore_anchors.definition: One of the two elite demon forces in the Immortal manor world, led by a powerful Loose Immortal known as Duohe the Immortal.

A superior variant of standard Dao-soldier armor, capable of forming a giant, translucent specter of a hunchbacked giant holding an iron fork; their appearance signals the Wu Jiang clan’s elite military force.

A cultivator who failed to transcend the Heavenly Tribulation and had to abandon their physical body, surviving as a soul-bound entity. They are extremely powerful but must periodically face increasingly deadly tribulations.

surfaces: waiting by the tree, watching for the rabbit
lore_anchors.definition: A famous Chinese fable idiom (守株待兔). In Xianxia strategy, it describes the tactic of predicting your opponent’s essential destination and setting an ambush there, turning patience into a weapon.

An ancient, chaotic being born from the primordial chaos, possessing immense size and raw power. Their bodies are their primary weapons, capable of feats far beyond human cultivators of similar energy levels.
A sacred vow made under the observation of the Heavenly Dao itself. Breaking such an oath carries severe karmic consequences and is considered binding upon both parties.
One of the five main halls of the Immortal manor, designed as a medicine garden for Wu Jiang the Immortal. It was guarded by golems and contained precious spiritual herbs.
Magical constructs, often made of metal or stone, animated by talismans or spells to serve as guardians or laborers. They lack independent thought and follow preset commands.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why are the demon forces so powerful?
cultural_notes_faq.a: They are descendants of the original tribe that served the Immortal manor’s master. Trapped for millennia, their soldiers are elite Dao-soldiers and their leaders are Loose Immortals, making them a serious threat even to top-tier cultivators.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why can’t Xiangliu Fang just fight them directly?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Xiangliu Fang is at peak Primal level with combat power comparable to a top Loose Immortal, but the demon armies have over ten thousand soldiers each, plus their own Loose Immortal leaders. Even he admitted the two strongest forces would beat him badly.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What’s a ‘waiting by the tree, watching for the rabbit’ tactic?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It’s a classic Xianxia trap: instead of chasing the enemy, you just guard the only place they have to go (the unrefined halls). The enemy knows it’s a trap, but they have to walk into it anyway because they can’t progress without doing so.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why didn’t the crew get the best Immortal herbs?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Xiangliu Fang is incredibly fast and ruthless. Before anyone could react, his giant hand transformed into serpents and plucked the eighteen best herbs. He is a Primordial Fiendgod with no concept of ‘sharing;’ to him, the strong take what they want.
